body:
## Problem
Redudant code. Related to #36112

## Solution
Combine `pathcmp()`, `path_fnamencmp()` and `path_fnamecmp()`.
Add a helper `path_fold_char()` to fold `\` and `/` as equal, and also consults 'fileignorecase'.

| feature                  | pathcmp        | path_fnamencmp | now          |
| ------------------------ | -------------- | -------------- | ------------ |
| case folding             | `mb_toupper()` | `utf_fold()`   | `utf_fold()` |
| consults &fileignorecase | ✅             | ✅             | ✅           |
| `maxlen`                 | ✅             | ✅             | ✅           |
| `/` == `\`               | ✅             | ✅             | ✅           |
| MSWIN drive letter       | ❌             | ✅             | ✅           |
| sep affects sorting      | ✅             | ❌             | ✅           |
| ignores a trailing slash | ✅             | ❌             | ✅           |

I checked all the callers of the three functions. Looks like these changes won't have any significant impact on them. As for `path_full_compare`, seems only `kEqualFiles` and `kEqualFileNames` are currently used. If needed, we could simplify it to return a bool? It would still require one call to `pathcmp` and two calls to `os_fileid`.

TODO:
audit callers again. Verify if new tests are needed, update comments and commit messages.

<!--
  Thank you for contributing to Neovim!
  If this is your first time, check out https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#pull-requests-prs
  for our PR guidelines.
-->

comment_data.body:
`path_cmp` ignoring a single trailing separator has a side effect here: it makes `exists('#BufRead#foo') == exists('#BufRead#foo/')`. However, the `autocmd-pattern` docs already state that `/` affects matching behavior. I haven't figured out why `path_fnamecmp` was used instead of something like `strcmp`; the [commit](https://github.com/vim/vim/commit/071d4279d6ab81b7187b48f3a0fc61e587b6db6c) is over 20 years old.
I'll run some more tests later to evaluate the actual impact.

comment_data.diff_hunk:
@@ -46,34 +47,39 @@ static inline uint32_t hash_cstr_t(const char *s)
 #define equal_cstr_t strequal
 
 /// Hash/equality for path strings. On case-insensitive platforms, case-fold first (via
-/// str_foldcase, the same fold used by mb_stricmp/path_fnamencmp) so the hash↔equality invariant
+/// path_fold_char, the same fold used by path_cmp) so the hash↔equality invariant
 /// holds.
 ///
-/// On Windows we additionally:
-///   - fold '\\' -> '/'   (path_fnamencmp treats them as equal)
-///   - drop a leading drive letter "[A-Za-z]:" so that "C:\foo" and "\foo" land in the same bucket
-///     (path_fnamencmp considers them equal when the current drive matches the explicit drive
-///     letter). Two paths with *different* explicit drives ("C:\foo" vs "D:\foo") may now
-///     share a bucket — that's a permitted collision; equal_path_t still rejects them.
+/// We additionally:
+///   - fold '\\' -> '/'   (path_fnamecmp treats them as equal on Windows)
+///   - drop a leading drive letter "[A-Za-z]:" on Windows, so that "C:\foo" and "\foo" land in
+///     the same bucket (path_fnamecmp considers them equal when the current drive matches the
+///     explicit drive letter). Two paths with *different* explicit drives ("C:\foo" vs "D:\foo")
+///     may now share a bucket — that's a permitted collision; equal_path_t still rejects them.
+///   - ignore a single trailing path separator.
 ///
-/// path_fnamencmp's non-Windows branch consults &fileignorecase, which is runtime-mutable and would
-/// break the hash invariant if flipped. So the macOS branch deliberately bypasses path_fnamencmp
-/// and uses the compile-time CASE_INSENSITIVE_FILENAME switch instead.
+/// Also, even in PR #40013, path_fnamecmp's Windows branch still consults &fileignorecase.
+/// So for now, we can directly use path_fnamecmp in equal_path_t.

comment_data.body: Not sure if `SIZE_MAX` is a bad choice. Just thought it should be sufficient, paths generally don't get this large. 😅

> However, the `autocmd-pattern` docs already state that `/` affects matching behavior.

Hmm, interesting. 

It could be argued that `pattern=foo/` may want to matches directories specifically, especially since https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/40552 strengthened the semantics recently. So it would be a step backwards to ignore that...

comment_data.body: those tests may be intentionally exceeding the limits

I switched to `mb_strcmp_ic` here. The only difference from the old `path_fnamecmp` is the separator handling, and `file-pattern` also states that path separators should use `/` on all platforms, so I assume this difference is acceptable. However, if this behavior is important, we can still normalize the separators in `pattern` to `/` beforehand.

comment_data.body:
switched to `MAXPATHL`.
BTW, I checked each migrated call site in the code and manually tested some to understand their behavior.
Today I also had GLM 5.2 review them. If needed, I can check tomorrow whether they already have some corresponding functional tests or need new ones to added. :D
>   Bottom line: solid refactor. The unification of
  pathcmp/path_fnamencmp/path_fnamecmp/path_full_compare into path_cmp + path_equal +
  path_fold_char is faithful — I traced every migrated call site and the semantics line up. Builds
  clean on MSVC, autocmd suite green. No correctness bugs found. Items below are polish + a       
  couple of latent/cosmetic things worth a decision.
